newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debt prices track U.S. Treasuries lower.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt prices track U.S. Treasuries lower.

text.p: Emerging debt prices ended the New York trading session lower across the board, tracking a weaker U.S. Treasury market, as underlying fears of a U.S. interest rake hike continue to loom over the market, traders said.

"People are worried about the Fed's next move, the Street's still seeing more net supply with a lack of buyside demand, but I'd say more than anything else its the U.S. Treasury market that's affecting prices," said one Brady trader.

On Monday, the yield on the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond shot up to 7.0 percent, but later pulled back to 6.96 percent in late session. At the close, the 30-year bond was off 5/32 at 95-27/32 to yield 6.96 percent.
Dealers said despite the rebound in the U.S. T-bond emerging debt prices remained weaker.
"The recovery of the bond towards the end of the day carried our market back up a bit, so we've recovered from the lows, but we're still down across the board," another Brady trader said.
Players said overall, trading was fairly thin and choppy with spreads seen wider by 15 to 20 basis points.
"There wasn't a lot of news out there today to trade on...if anything we just tracked the U.S. Treasury bond one-for-one," he added.
Venezuela PARs fell 5/8 to 72-1/8 bid and Venezuela FLIRBs traded off 1/2 to 87-1/8 bid. Mexico Pars fell 3/8 to 72-1/2 bid and Discounts were off 1/2 at 88-1/8 bid.
Also, Argentina Pars were unchanged at 64-1/4 bid, FRBs, however, traded off 1/2 at 89-3/8 bid. Brazil C also fell 3/4 to 76-1/4 bid.
Russia Vnesh US$ was also quoted off 1/4 at 81-1/2 bid.
Meanwhile, Bulgaria debt stood alone as the only gainer on the day.

On Monday, The International Monetary Fund (IMF) and Bulgaria's interim cabinet announced an accord on financial reform and funding worth more than $650 million to stabilize the shattered economy over the next year.

"That was very good news for Bulgaria it drove prices as high as two points but later gave way to pretty agressive profit-taking," said one debt trader. "IABs are now 2-1/4 points off earlier highs reached this morning."
Bulgaria FLRB wound down the New York trading session unchanged at 45 bid, IABs ended 1/4 higher at a 60 bid, off earlier highs, traders said.
Still players said an underlying concern going forward is the U.S. interest picture as fears of a potential hike in interest rates continues to weigh down prices, dealers said.
The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), the policy setting arm of the Federal Reserve Board is expected to meet on March 25th to discuss monetary policy.
